questions.stem: The permanent Secretariat of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), established in 1985, is located in which city?

options.option_text: New Delhi, the political hub of India in South Asia
Colombo, the commercial hub of Sri Lanka
Kathmandu, the capital city of Nepal
Dhaka, the capital city of Bangladesh

questions.explanation: The SAARC Secretariat was established in Kathmandu, Nepal in 1987, two years after the organisation was founded in Dhaka. New Delhi is the most common wrong answer because India is the largest SAARC member, but the secretariat was deliberately placed in a smaller member nation to balance political influence across the region.

questions.stem: The World Trade Organization came into existence on 1 January 1995, formally replacing which predecessor body that had governed international trade rules since 1948?

options.option_text: GATT — General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, signed in 1947
UNCTAD — United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
ITO — International Trade Organization, proposed but never ratified
OECD — Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development

questions.explanation: GATT (1947) served as the provisional framework governing global trade for nearly 50 years until the WTO replaced it after the Uruguay Round. ITO is the classic distractor — it was the originally intended institution that the US Congress refused to ratify in 1950, so GATT became the de facto stop-gap. UNCTAD and OECD serve entirely different functions.

questions.stem: The Kimberley Process Certification Scheme, launched in 2003 with governments, industry, and civil society, was specifically designed to halt the illicit trade in which commodity?

options.option_text: Raw ivory obtained through illegal elephant poaching
Illegally harvested tropical timber and forest products
Protected marine species including coral and fish
Rough diamonds mined to fund armed conflicts and rebellions

questions.explanation: The Kimberley Process targets 'conflict diamonds' or 'blood diamonds' — rough diamonds whose sale finances rebel movements fighting legitimate governments, as seen devastatingly in Angola and Sierra Leone during the 1990s. Ivory trafficking is regulated separately under CITES, making it the most tempting wrong choice since both involve illicit natural-resource trade.

questions.stem: INTERPOL, the world's largest international police cooperation organisation with 196 member countries, maintains its General Secretariat in which city?

options.option_text: Paris, the capital and diplomatic centre of France
Lyon, a major industrial city in south-eastern France
Brussels, the administrative centre of the European Union
Geneva, the seat of numerous UN specialized agencies

questions.explanation: INTERPOL's General Secretariat has been in Lyon, France since 1989, when it relocated from Saint-Cloud near Paris. Paris is the most common wrong answer since it is France's capital, but INTERPOL deliberately positioned itself away from political centres. Geneva is a plausible distractor given the concentration of international bodies headquartered there.

questions.stem: The ASEAN Secretariat, which coordinates the work of the bloc founded by the Bangkok Declaration of 1967, is permanently based in which city?

options.option_text: Bangkok, the Thai capital where ASEAN was originally founded in 1967
Singapore, the prosperous city-state and ASEAN financial hub
Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia and ASEAN's most populous member
Kuala Lumpur, the Malaysian capital in the heart of ASEAN

questions.explanation: The ASEAN Secretariat has been located in Jakarta, Indonesia since its establishment in 1976. Indonesia, being the largest ASEAN member by population and territory, hosts it. Bangkok is the most tempting wrong answer since ASEAN was founded there in 1967 — candidates confuse founding city with secretariat location, a distinction examiners frequently test.

questions.stem: The UN Trusteeship Council, one of the six principal organs of the United Nations, formally suspended its operations in November 1994. Which event directly triggered this historic suspension?

options.option_text: Palau, the last remaining UN trust territory, gained independence from the US
Namibia achieved independence in 1990, completing Africa's decolonization
The Soviet Union's dissolution ended the Cold War-era mandate system
The General Assembly voted to merge Trusteeship with ECOSOC functions

questions.explanation: Palau became independent on 1 October 1994 after ending its status as the last UN Strategic Trust Territory under US administration, triggering the Council's suspension on 1 November 1994. Namibia (Option B) is the most dangerous distractor — it did achieve independence in 1990, but it was administered under a League of Nations mandate disputed by South Africa, not a formal UN trust territory. Palau held that last-trust-territory distinction.

questions.stem: Under Article 108 of the UN Charter, an amendment enters into force when ratified by two-thirds of all UN members, but only if one additional binding condition is satisfied. What is that condition?

options.option_text: At least three of the five permanent Security Council members must approve it
The International Court of Justice must certify the amendment as legally binding
The UN Secretary-General must formally endorse and gazette the amendment
All five permanent members of the Security Council must ratify it too

questions.explanation: Article 108 requires the two-thirds majority AND ratification by all five permanent members (US, UK, France, Russia, China), effectively giving each P5 nation a veto over any Charter amendment — not just Security Council resolutions. Option A ('at least three of five') is the classic distractor: candidates confuse the Charter amendment threshold with the Security Council's procedural voting rules, where nine votes (including all P5 concurrence) are needed.
